Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party No.1 instituted Title Suit No.249 of 1984 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kurigram for declaration of title on correction of record of right. Plaintiff's case in short is that the suit land originally belonged to Ibrahim Sheikh and Ishaque Sheikh in equal 8 annas share. Ibrahim Sheikh died leaving two sons Azizur Rahman and Insar Ali who inherited him. Ishaque Sheikh died leaving only son Nizamuddin who inherited 8 annas share of his father in the suit property. Nizamuddin died leaving wife Habija Bewa and daughter Hasina Banu. During possession they sold 4.49 decimals of land to Alauddin vide registered kabala dated 08.01.1948. In his turn Alauddin transferred 3.17 decimals of land to the plaintiff vide registered patta taking salami of taka 970/-. Khatian No.64 wrongly 4 recorded in the name of defendants. Plaintiff came to know about the wrong recording when he went to pay rent to the Tahasil office. Hence, the present suit. 

 6. Mr. Md. Mosiul Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submit that the courts below failed to consider that the patta executed on 24 Falgun 1354 B.S. by Alauddin in favour of the plaintiff was for a limited period and the Patta was not executed by both lessee and lessor and as such it is 'not a valid patta. He submits that the plaintiff produced certified copy of the patta without any explanation as to the original of the same and as such accepting the secondary evidence is not proper and legal. He also submits that the plaintiff filed suit for declaration without seeking any consequential relief and as such the suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. He submits that a patta unless executed by both the lessor and lessee is void under Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act and without considering this legal aspect the appellate court below committed an error of law which occasioned failure of justice. He also submits that the impugned judgment and decree is bad for non-consideration of the material evidence and misreading of evidence on record and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He submits that the revisional court is competent to interfere in a case of non-consideration of material evidence which is specifically material for determination of the material issue. He further submits that the plaintiff neither avail to record their names in the Record of Rights nor they have proved their tenancy as a holding over and without considering this legal aspect the appellate court below committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice. In support of his submissions, the learned Advocate referred to the case of Abdus Sattar and others vs. Suresh Chandra Das and others, reported in 32 DLR (AD) 170; the case of Syed Imteyazuddin Hossain vs. Md. Abdul Majid, reported in 22 DLR 451; Sheikh Md. Siddique vs. Hari Lal Nath and others, reported in 22 DLR 359; the case of Narendra Nath Pal vs. Abdur Rahman Molla, reported in 26 DLR 45; the case of Noor Mohammad Khan and others vs. Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others, reported in 42 DLR 434; the case of Dudu Mia and other vs. Ekram Miah Chowdhury and others, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 7; the case of Bina Rani and another vs. Shantosh Chandra Dey, reported in 51 DLR(AD) 81 and the case of Safaruddin and others vs. Fazlul Huq and others, reported in 49 DLR (AD) 151. 

 11. It appears that both the parties admits that Alauddin, predecessor of the defendants, settled the suit land to the plaintiff vide registered patta. Discord between the parties started thereafter. Plaintiff claims that he took settlement of the land vide registered patta and since then he is in possession of the suit land. He further claims that due to illness the plaintiff could not appear before the settlement employees during last survey and as such S.A. Khatian No.64 wrongly recorded in the name of defendants and he came to know about the wrong recording when he went to pay rent to the Tahasil Office. On the other hand the definite case of the defendant Nos.1-3 is that plaintiff surrendered the suit land in 1360 B.S. by giving ishtafanama being unable to pay rent and since then the defendants are in possession of the suit land. S.A. Khatian prepared accordingly. I have carefully and meticulously gone through the judgment passed by the courts below. It appears that the learned Assistant Judge after framing proper issues and after threadbare discussions on the issues arrived at a finding : 

 13. The submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the patta was not executed by both parties and it is for a limited period are beyond the pleadings of the case and as such the same is not require to be addressed in this revisional jurisdiction.
